The electrical conductivity of pure PVDF is approximately 10^-16 S/m.
Adding 2 wt.% MnO2 nanotubes to PVDF increases conductivity to about 10^-5 S/m.
Incorporating 1 wt.% f-MWCNTs into 5 wt.% MNTs/PVDF composite raises conductivity to approximately 10^-1 S/m.
EMI shielding effectiveness of ~20 dB was achieved with 5 wt.% MNTs and 1 wt.% f-MWCNTs in PVDF at X-band frequencies.
7 wt.% f-MWCNTs in PVDF alone yield an EMI SE of about 18 dB, lower than the hybrid composite with less CNT content.
MnO2 nanotubes synthesized hydrothermally have diameters of 50-70 nm and micron lengths.
Functionalized MWCNTs have diameters of 30-40 nm and lengths around 10 microns.
FTIR confirmed hydroxyl and carboxyl functional groups on f-MWCNTs.
Raman spectroscopy showed increased defect density in f-MWCNTs compared to purified MWCNTs.
FESEM images demonstrated homogeneous dispersion of MNTs and f-MWCNTs in PVDF matrix.
Chemical resistance tests showed 95-100% resistance of composites to acids, bases, organic solvents, and alkanes.
XRD confirmed the crystalline phases of PVDF, MnO2 nanotubes, and f-MWCNTs without impurities.
The main EMI shielding mechanism in these composites is reflection.
The composites were prepared by ultrasonication, solvent casting, and hot pressing into 1 mm thick films.
EMI SE was measured using a vector network analyzer with an X-band waveguide sample holder.
The addition of MNTs helps overcome Van der Waals forces between f-MWCNTs, improving dispersion.
The hybrid filler system reduces the required loading of expensive carbon nanotubes for effective EMI shielding.
The composites exhibit a percolation behavior in electrical conductivity with increasing filler loading.
The study focuses on low-cost EMI shielding materials suitable for X-band applications such as military and telecommunication devices.
The polymer matrix molecular weight used was 100,000 g/mol PVDF.
